questions.stem: A JSON column holds nested objects. Which SQL syntax reads a nested field from a string column raw?
questions.explanation: The colon syntax `<column>:<path>` extracts fields from JSON strings, with dots for nested fields.

questions.stem: Which function turns each element of an array column into its own row?
questions.explanation: explode returns a set of rows by un-nesting the collection.

questions.stem: How do you read JSON files that each contain one record spread over many lines?

options.text: Set the multiLine option to true

questions.explanation: By default the JSON reader expects one record per line; multiLine reads records that span lines.

questions.stem: A connector lands semi-structured payloads whose fields vary by record. Which approach keeps them without losing fields?

options.text: Drop records whose fields don't match
Store them in a VARIANT column and extract fields when needed

questions.explanation: Databricks recommends VARIANT over JSON strings for semi-structured data; fields are extracted when queried.

questions.stem: A JSON string column raw holds an object store with a key bicycle. Besides raw:store.bicycle, which syntax also reads it?
questions.explanation: After the colon, a path can use dots or brackets with the key in quotes.
